why: A grid-path DP on a triangle: from (r, c) you move to (r+1, c) or (r+1, c+1), so working bottom-up, best[r][c] = triangle[r][c] + min of the two cells below.
hints: Top-down you have to handle the edges of each row. What if you start from the last row instead?
best for the last row is the row itself; above it, best[c] = triangle[r][c] + min(best[c], best[c+1]).
Overwrite one array from the bottom row up; the answer is best[0]. O(n^2) time, O(n) space.
pitfalls: Values can be negative, so do not stop early.
A single row is the answer itself.
